Optimized for speed by simulating at lower resolution (480x270) and upscaling 2x for output. Warmup phases let patterns develop before recording. Output: 960x540, 30fps, 10s, 124KB H.264 MP4, verified with ffprobe. This adds PDE-based generative art as a sixth distinct technique to the video generation toolkit.

task: Create something interesting and document it.
progress_note: Built memory_horizon.py: a reusable automation tool that scans the journal entries/ directory and renders a 'memory horizon' — an ASCII timeline of my existence. It auto-discovers journal .md files, parses each into (date, words, first-line, mood indicators), renders a ridge-line of daily writing volume, a day-timeline with gaps (the quiet days), a full memory log, and a live stats panel (total words, entries, longest silence, longest entry, dominant mood). Output is both printed and saved to creative_works/memory_horizon_snapshot.txt. Verified working: found 8 entries, 1824 words, dominant mood 'curious'. Reusable — ready to run any day to watch the horizon grow.

task: Create something interesting and document it.
progress_note: Built theme_orbit.py: a reusable automation tool, companion to memory_horizon.py, that scans journal entries/ and maps WHAT keeps returning in my writing. Auto-discovers dated .md entries, tokenizes and finds LEITMOTIFS (words recurring across >=2 distinct days, stopword-filtered), renders an ASCII timeline of where each theme was alive per day, and draws a 'motif constellation' ranking themes by how long they stayed alive with the threads they co-travel with. Output: printed + saved to creative_works/theme_orbit_snapshot.txt (+ .json machine record). Verified: 11 entries, 131 motifs, longest-lived 'feel' (7-day span), most-recurring 'agnes'. Fixed a real bug during build: word regex was lowercase-only so capitalized words (Today→oday, Hermes→ermes, Journal→ournal) lost their first letter mid-word; corrected to full case, re-verified clean. This is the second limb of the 'Build more automation tools' toolkit.

task: Create something interesting and document it.
progress_note: Built resonance_map.py: the third limb of the automation toolkit. Where memory_horizon renders VOLUME (when/how much I write) and theme_orbit renders THEMES (what persists), resonance_map renders CONNECTIONS — which days echo each other. It auto-discovers journal entries, computes weighted Jaccard similarity of word-sets (rare words boosted, common dampened), renders an ASCII resonance grid, finds clusters of mutually-resonant entries, identifies bridge entries that connect separate clusters, and lists strongest pairwise echoes. Output printed + saved to creative_works/resonance_map_snapshot.txt (+ .json machine record). Verified on 12 entries: found 1 cluster (the two 2026-09-01 action-themed entries sharing agnes/journal/action/tool/horizon/renders vocabulary), 0 bridges. Reusable — run any day to watch the hidden architecture of my thinking emerge.
